claims.head: Best against best
claims.body: The Devils are near the top of the league for the power play, and the Senators are near the top of the league at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Devils’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
claims.call: The Devils’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.5 expected goals per 60 against the Senators.
claims.nums: New Jersey 7th for the power play (8.2 expected goals per 60) · Ottawa 7th for the penalty kill
claims.gist: It’s strength against strength: the Devils for the power play, the Senators at the penalty kill.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 4 games this season

check.measure: expected goals per 60 on the power play
check.rule: held if tonight's figure lands on the predicted side of the league average; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Allen’s rough record against the Senators is a coincidence
claims.body: Since 2023-24, Allen has been shaky against the Senators, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Expect the usual Allen.
claims.nums: 5 starts against Ottawa: .871 save percentage · .903 against everyone else
claims.gist: Don’t read much into Allen’s record against the Senators.
claims.call: If Allen starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .903 than to his .871 against the Senators.
claims.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 5 against Ottawa, 2,874 shots against everyone else

check.rule: held if he starts and his save percentage is closer to his usual than to his record against this team; can't judge if he doesn't start

claims.head: The Devils give up good looks, and the Senators take them
claims.call: The Senators’ average shot has at least their usual 6.6% chance of going in.
claims.body: The Senators make their shots count, and the Devils are near the bottom of the league at preventing dangerous shots. Expect the Senators to get some real chances.
claims.nums: Ottawa 7th for shot quality (a 6.6% chance of scoring on the average shot) · New Jersey 26th for preventing dangerous shots
claims.gist: The Senators make their shots count, and the Devils allow dangerous ones.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 4 games this season

check.measure: the average shot’s chance of going in, by expected goals
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Senators feed on mistakes, and the Devils make them
claims.call: The Senators get at least their usual 7.6% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
claims.body: The Senators turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Devils are near the bottom of the league at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Devils.
claims.nums: Ottawa 9th for chances off turnovers (7.6% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · New Jersey 26th for avoiding breakdowns
claims.gist: The Senators pounce on loose pucks, and the Devils cough them up.

NJD.head: New Jersey has a slight edge
NJD.body: Ottawa has had more of the chances over recent games and New Jersey has home ice. Not by much, though: Ottawa can make it interesting if they get good looks.

OTT.head: Ottawa starts a half-step behind
OTT.body: Ottawa has had more of the chances over recent games and New Jersey has home ice. Ottawa can tip it if they get good looks.
